name: dig
title: Query DNS records
description: Performs DNS lookups and prints the full answer, including which nameserver replied. The standard tool for diagnosing 'the domain does not resolve' problems.
aliases: what ip does this domain point to

flags.name: +short
flags.description: Print only the answer, with no metadata.

flags.name: +trace
flags.description: Trace delegation from the root nameservers down.

flags.name: @server
flags.description: Query a specific nameserver instead of the system resolver.

examples.explanation: Prints just the A records for the domain.
Looks up the mail exchanger records.

name: nslookup
title: Look up DNS names and addresses
description: Queries DNS for a domain or IP address. Less detailed than dig but available by default on Windows as well as most Unix systems.
aliases: find the ip of a website

flags.name: -type
flags.description: Query a specific record type, e.g. -type=MX.

examples.explanation: Resolves the domain to its IP addresses.

name: traceroute
title: Trace the network path to a host
description: Shows each router hop between you and a destination along with the latency at each step, which helps locate where a connection slows down or fails. On Windows the equivalent is 'tracert'.
aliases: trace the route to a server
find where the connection is slow

flags.name: -n
flags.description: Show numeric addresses without reverse DNS lookups, which is faster.

flags.name: -m
flags.description: Set the maximum number of hops to probe.

examples.explanation: Shows every hop on the path to the host.

risk.sideEffects: Sends probe packets; read-only with respect to local state.

name: ip
title: Show and configure network interfaces
description: The modern Linux tool for inspecting and configuring addresses, links, and routes. It replaces the deprecated ifconfig and route commands.

examples.explanation: Lists every interface with its assigned addresses.

risk.sideEffects: The 'show' subcommands are read-only. Subcommands such as 'ip addr add' modify network configuration and require root.
risk.reversibility: Configuration changes are reversible but can drop a remote session.

name: ipconfig
title: Show Windows network configuration
description: Displays the IP address, subnet mask, and gateway for each Windows network adapter, and can renew DHCP leases or flush the DNS cache.
aliases: what is my ip on windows

flags.name: /all
flags.description: Show full configuration including MAC addresses and DNS servers.

flags.name: /flushdns
flags.description: Clear the local DNS resolver cache.

examples.explanation: Shows the complete configuration for every adapter.

risk.sideEffects: /all is read-only. /renew and /flushdns change network state and may briefly interrupt connectivity.
risk.reversibility: Changes are transient and re-established automatically.

name: ssh
title: Connect to a remote host over SSH
description: Opens an encrypted shell session on a remote machine. Anything you then run executes on that remote host, not locally.

flags.name: -i
flags.description: Use a specific private key file.

flags.name: -L
flags.description: Forward a local port to a port on the remote side.

examples.explanation: Opens a shell on the remote host as the deploy user.
Connects using a specific key and port.

risk.sideEffects: Opens an interactive session on a remote system; subsequent commands affect that host.
risk.reversibility: Ending the session is reversible, but actions taken on the remote host are not.

name: scp
title: Copy files over SSH
description: Copies files between hosts over an SSH connection. It silently overwrites the destination if a file with that name already exists.
aliases: copy a file to a server
download a file from a server

flags.name: -P
flags.description: Connect to a non-default SSH port (uppercase P).

examples.explanation: Uploads a local file to the remote /tmp directory.

risk.sideEffects: Writes files on the destination, overwriting same-named files without prompting.

name: wget
title: Download files from the web
description: Downloads files over HTTP, HTTPS, and FTP. Unlike curl it writes to a file by default and can resume interrupted transfers.
aliases: get a file from the internet

flags.name: -O
flags.description: Write output to the given filename.

flags.name: -q
flags.description: Quiet mode with no progress output.

examples.explanation: Downloads the file into the current directory.

risk.sideEffects: Writes downloaded files to disk and makes outbound network requests.
risk.reversibility: Reversible by deleting the downloaded file.
